entries.17cb228ba877fbc4: A company that makes automotive interior components such as seats and door trims, and parts such as filters, and supplies them mainly to the [[company:toyota|Toyota Motor]] group.
entries.1c90118b2c8d958f: This is a business in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Brazil and Argentina. Toyota Boshoku America Co., Ltd. (Kentucky, USA) oversees the business, and subsidiaries in Tennessee, Indiana, Illinois and Kentucky in the United States, Ontario in Canada, and the city of Buenos Aires in Argentina, among others, have production facilities for automotive parts. Toyota Boshoku America Co., Ltd.'s revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (excluding internal revenue between consolidated companies) was ¥513,360 million, and it is a company whose share of consolidated revenue exceeds 10%. Revenue from external customers in the North, Central and South America segment was ¥537,656 million (up 11.1% year on year), second only to Japan in scale. The company explains that revenue increased due to growth in production volumes and changes in model mix.
entries.57d3f934006e62c6: This is a business in China. Toyoda Boshoku (China) Ltd. (Shanghai) oversees the business, and subsidiaries including Tianjin Eitai Automotive Trim Ltd., Tianjin Toyoda Boshoku Automotive Parts Ltd., and Toyoda Boshoku (Tianjin) Automotive Parts Ltd. (all in Tianjin), and Guangzhou Ōtai Automotive Trim Ltd. and Toyoda Boshoku (Guangzhou) Automotive Parts Ltd. (both in Guangzhou, Guangdong Province), as well as subsidiaries in Chengdu, Ningbo, Foshan and Shenyang, among others, are in the automotive parts business. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥202,377 million (down 8.9% year on year). The company explains that revenue decreased due to a decline in production volumes, among other factors.
entries.587480dd897c5cde: Toyota Motor Corporation and its group companies
entries.881a86d019493995: This is a business in Japan. TOYOTA BOSHOKU CORPORATION (the company) is in charge, and at factories in Aichi and Gifu prefectures and elsewhere it manufactures interior components such as automotive seats, door trims and molded headliners, and unit parts such as filters and motor cores for hybrid systems. Domestic subsidiaries include Toyota Boshoku Tohoku Co., Ltd. (Kitakami, Iwate Prefecture), Toyota Boshoku Kyushu Co., Ltd. (Kanzaki, Saga Prefecture), Toyota Boshoku Seiko Co., Ltd. (Takahama, Aichi Prefecture), Araco Co., Ltd., Toyota Boshoku Hirose Co., Ltd., Koberuku Co., Ltd., and TB Logistics Co., Ltd., which handles transportation. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥891,184 million (up 3.2% year on year), the largest region among the five reportable segments. The company explains that revenue increased due to the introduction of new products, among other factors. The main customer is [[company:toyota|TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION]] and its group companies; of the group's revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026, sales to TOYOTA MOTOR CORPORATION were ¥478,328 million and sales to Toyota Auto Body Co., Ltd. were ¥204,578 million.
entries.f91000cf4ed4393b: This is a business in Thailand, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Vietnam and others. Toyota Boshoku Asia Co., Ltd. (Bangkok, Thailand) oversees the region to strengthen an optimal production and supply structure and a structure closely aligned with local regions. Toyota Boshoku Indonesia Co., Ltd., STB Textiles Industry Co., Ltd., Toyota Boshoku Filtration Systems (Thailand) Co., Ltd. and Toyota Boshoku Siam Metal Co., Ltd. (all in Thailand), Toyota Boshoku Device India Co., Ltd. (India), Toyota Boshoku Haiphong Ltd. (Vietnam), Toyota Boshoku Philippines Co., Ltd. and others are in charge of the automotive parts business. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥285,145 million (up 5.9% year on year), larger than China and second only to Japan and North, Central and South America. The company explains that revenue increased due to growth in production volumes and the effects of exchange rates.
entries.ff660ff3eb5b10fe: This is a business in France, Poland, Slovakia, Turkey, South Africa and others. Toyota Boshoku Europe Co., Ltd. (Belgium) oversees the business, and subsidiaries including Toyota Boshoku Poland Ltd., Toyota Boshoku Turkey Co., Ltd., Toyota Boshoku Soman Co., Ltd. (France) and Toyota Boshoku South Africa Co., Ltd. are in charge of the automotive parts business. Revenue from external customers for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥120,698 million (up 4.6% year on year), the smallest region among the five reportable segments. The company explains that revenue increased due to the effects of exchange rates, among other factors.
